reasons: The cited paragraphs confirm the gap: Section 9 grants only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and trigger-based (9.3) termination rights, and Section 8.1/8.2 commit Customer to a three-year term with automatic 12-month renewals, so there is no Customer convenience exit — walk-away territory under T4C and a correct 'missing' classification.

The inserted language tracks the rule's model language closely: 30 days' written notice, whole or partial termination, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination fee, and confirmation that Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right (consistent with the preferred position and with the existing document, which gives Vendor none).
The edit is additive and minimal — no existing clause text is altered — and it is placed logically in Section 9 (the vacant 9.4 slot); consider numbering the new sentence '9.4' for clean integration.
The comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 60-day fallback; deterministic checks confirm the Customer convenience right is present.
